Producing Intelligence at a Glance: How Llama 3 405B Was Made, End to End

One AI factory, one model, nine stages. This page puts the whole Producing Intelligence series on one map, following Meta's Llama 3 405B from the software that runs a 16,384-GPU cluster to the operations team that keeps it alive. Click any stage for its key number, the decision Meta made, the main risk and the tools involved, then jump to the full article.

Explore the pipeline ↓ Start at Part 1 →
The pipeline Timeline Where the compute went Decision map Follow one GPU-hour Key numbers Reading tracks Glossary
⚠️ About these numbers. Every figure on this page comes from one of the nine articles in the series and inherits that article's sources and caveats. Most come from Meta's paper "The Llama 3 Herd of Models" (arXiv 2407.21783) and Meta's engineering posts; items marked ⚠️ come from secondary sources. Where Meta did not publish a number (for example, post-training GPU-hours), we say so instead of estimating.

🏭 The pipeline

Read from the top down: infrastructure and data come first, the training run turns compute into a base model, post-training and evaluation turn it into a product, and serving and operations keep it running.

🗓️ The Llama 3 405B timeline

The order of work, from cluster to release. Meta published dates only for some milestones; the rest are shown in sequence without dates.

⚡ Where the compute went

The published GPU-hour figures, on the same scale. Pre-training dominates the published numbers; Meta did not publish GPU-hours for post-training, evaluation or serving, so those appear as labelled gaps.

Sources: Llama 3 paper and model card (30.84M H100-hours for 405B pre-training; 39.3M for the Llama 3.1 family; 8,930 t CO₂ location-based). See Part 3.

🧭 Decision map

At every stage Meta chose one option among several. The table shows the choice, the main alternative and why it fitted Llama 3. Click a row to open the article.
